chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn 'Uthman from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sent his hunting dog, and it caught game, and the dog ate from it; should I eat from its surplus? He said: Eat whatever the dog killed, if you named it (God), and if you were forgetful, then eat from it as well, and eat its surplus.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat game caught by a dog that has eaten part of it?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Isfahar, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of consuming game caught by a trained hunting dog, emphasizing that the act of naming God (Tasmiyah) upon sending the dog is the decisive condition. The ruling applies whether the hunter remembers the invocation or forgets it, and explicitly permits eating the 'fadhlah' (the portion the dog consumed), distinguishing this from the general rule where the dog's consumption might render the meat impure or less desirable. This highlights the Shia juristic view on the efficacy of Tasmiyah in hunting and the practical implications for hunters regarding waste and consumption.
